name: Gir
description: One of India’s best-known indigenous dairy breeds, Gir cattle are prized for rich milk, long productive life, and strong heat tolerance in semi-arid conditions.
milkYieldInfo: Typical milk yield ranges from 10 to 16 liters a day with good management. Milk is known for a high fat percentage and steady lactation across tropical climates.
feedingGuide: Provide dry fodder, green fodder, and 2 to 3 kg concentrate during peak lactation. Access to clean water, mineral mixture, and shade is essential for stable output.
careTips: Vaccinate on schedule for FMD, HS, and BQ. Deworm twice a year and watch udder hygiene closely in humid weather.
economicValue: Gir cattle command premium prices for breeding and dairy, especially in A2 milk-focused farms and climate-stress regions.

name: Sahiwal
description: Sahiwal is a top indigenous dairy breed valued for calm temperament, efficient feed conversion, and reliable milk yield under hot conditions.
milkYieldInfo: Average yield is 8 to 14 liters per day, with some elite animals performing much higher under organized dairy systems.
feedingGuide: Use balanced green fodder, legume hay, and concentrate linked to milk output. Add bypass protein and minerals for high-yielding animals.
careTips: Maintain fly control and clean housing. Sahiwal adapts well to heat, but lactating cows still benefit from cooling and frequent water access.
economicValue: A strong choice for small and medium dairy farms due to lower maintenance cost and good resale value for milch animals.

name: Red Sindhi
description: Red Sindhi cattle are hardy dairy animals known for adaptability, moderate milk production, and resilience in warm and dry environments.
milkYieldInfo: Most animals yield 6 to 10 liters daily, with better performance where feed quality and parasite control are consistent.
feedingGuide: Offer mixed fodder with extra protein during early lactation. Dry periods should include mineral supplementation and adequate roughage.
careTips: These cattle handle heat well but need parasite monitoring. Maintain hoof health on rough and rocky grazing land.
economicValue: Useful in low-input dairy systems where survival, fertility, and consistent moderate output matter more than peak yield.

name: Tharparkar
description: Tharparkar is a desert-adapted dual-purpose breed appreciated for milk production, drought endurance, and utility in dryland farming.
milkYieldInfo: Typical yield stays between 6 and 10 liters a day. Performance remains comparatively stable even in harsh summer conditions.
feedingGuide: Fibrous fodder is tolerated well, but lactating cows respond strongly to green fodder, oil cakes, and mineral bricks.
careTips: Provide protection from sand-laden winds and ensure water availability. Vaccination and tick control remain important in open grazing systems.
economicValue: Valuable for mixed farms needing both milk and resilient breeding stock adapted to scarce-resource environments.

name: Ongole
description: Ongole is a powerful zebu breed famous for muscular build, draught strength, and global influence in tropical beef and breeding programs.
milkYieldInfo: Milk output is modest, generally 3 to 6 liters a day, since the breed is primarily selected for size and work capacity.
feedingGuide: Use crop residues, dry fodder, and energy supplementation for working animals. Young stock benefit from protein-rich rations for frame development.
careTips: Exercise, hoof care, and parasite control are important due to large body size. Avoid prolonged standing in muddy yards.
economicValue: Strong value in breeding, draught, and conservation programs. Bulls are especially prized for size and hardiness.

name: Kankrej
description: Kankrej cattle combine respectable milk yield with strong draught ability, making them a classic dual-purpose breed in western India.
milkYieldInfo: Daily milk yield commonly ranges from 5 to 9 liters. Better housing and ration balancing can noticeably improve lactation performance.
feedingGuide: Feed green fodder, dry roughage, and concentrates in line with work or lactation demand. Salt and mineral access should be regular.
careTips: Kankrej does well in hot climates but needs clean flooring and careful tick management during monsoon periods.
economicValue: A versatile breed for farms balancing dairy income with breeding, bullock power, and long-term adaptability.

name: Hariana
description: Hariana cattle are known for compact frames, efficient work output, and dependable performance across northern Indian mixed farming systems.
milkYieldInfo: Most animals produce 4 to 8 liters a day while still retaining good usefulness as bullocks in traditional agriculture.
feedingGuide: Maintain roughage-heavy diets with concentrate support for milch cows. Field-working animals need extra energy and salt replacement.
careTips: Provide clean resting space and watch for heat stress during north Indian dry summers. Vaccination and deworming remain standard.
economicValue: Economically useful where farmers need one breed for both milk and field support rather than specialized high-input dairy animals.

name: Rathi
description: Rathi cattle are adaptable desert dairy animals with attractive coat patterns, good fertility, and strong performance in arid regions.
milkYieldInfo: Milk yield typically ranges from 6 to 10 liters daily. They are favored in semi-intensive systems across western India.
feedingGuide: Dry fodder and grazing can be supplemented with concentrate and mineral mixture to maintain body condition during lactation.
careTips: Shade and clean water are vital in hot zones. Monitor body condition closely during dry periods with sparse fodder availability.
economicValue: A reliable indigenous dairy option for dryland regions where resilience and reproductive efficiency improve farm stability.

name: Brown Swiss
description: Brown Swiss cattle are globally respected dairy animals known for steady production, strong feet and legs, and long productive life under structured farm management.
milkYieldInfo: Typical milk production ranges from 15 to 24 liters per day, with stable lactation and good solids that suit commercial dairy systems.
feedingGuide: Use high-quality green fodder, dry roughage, and balanced dairy concentrate. Consistent mineral support and clean water are important for sustained production.
careTips: Maintain cooling, hoof care, and clean housing. Because Brown Swiss cattle are larger-framed, comfortable flooring and dry resting areas improve longevity.
economicValue: Useful for organized dairy farms and crossbreeding programs where reliable yield, calm temperament, and durability are important.

name: Deoni
description: Deoni is a balanced dual-purpose breed valued for medium milk yield, body strength, and suitability for southern plateau conditions.
milkYieldInfo: Most Deoni cows produce 5 to 9 liters per day. Their performance is dependable where feeding is steady and disease pressure is managed.
feedingGuide: Use sorghum stover, legumes, and measured concentrate during lactation. Calcium and phosphorus support are useful for productive animals.
careTips: Maintain vaccination and tick control. Deoni cattle benefit from dry bedding and ventilation during humid monsoon months.
economicValue: Attractive for farmers needing a durable breed with both dairying and breeding utility in semi-intensive systems.

name: Holstein Friesian
description: Holstein Friesian cattle are among the highest-yielding dairy animals used in India, especially in intensive and crossbred milk production systems.
milkYieldInfo: Well-managed animals commonly produce 18 to 30 liters a day, with elite animals going higher under professional dairy management.
feedingGuide: Require high-energy fodder, quality silage, protein-rich concentrate, and regular mineral supplementation to support high milk output.
careTips: These cattle benefit from cooling, strict udder hygiene, and careful metabolic monitoring because high production can increase health stress.
economicValue: A major commercial dairy choice where high milk volume and organized feeding systems can support premium output.

name: Malvi
description: Malvi is a compact and energetic draught breed of central India, appreciated for movement, stamina, and low upkeep under farm conditions.
milkYieldInfo: Milk production is modest at 2 to 5 liters per day, reflecting selection mainly for field performance rather than dairy specialization.
feedingGuide: Crop residues and grazing form the base diet. Working animals should receive additional grain or concentrate before heavy workloads.
careTips: Prevent overwork in peak summer and keep hooves trimmed for hard-soil traction. Standard vaccination remains essential.
economicValue: Useful where bullock work still matters and low-cost maintenance is a priority for smallholder farms.

name: Nimari
description: Nimari cattle are small to medium draught animals suited to hot, dry tracts and valued for hardiness more than milk production.
milkYieldInfo: Yield is generally 2 to 4 liters a day and mostly supports household use rather than commercial dairying.
feedingGuide: Works well on grazing and roughage-heavy diets. Working animals should be supported with concentrate and electrolytes in hot weather.
careTips: Monitor for dehydration in summer and keep housing dry. Tick control and annual vaccination remain basic priorities.
economicValue: Best suited to low-input rural systems where resilience and draught support outweigh dairy income expectations.

name: Dangi
description: Dangi cattle are rain-zone survivors known for sure-footed movement, working ability, and adaptation to hilly and high-rainfall regions.
milkYieldInfo: Daily milk yield usually falls between 3 and 6 liters, making the breed more useful as a rugged dual-purpose option than a pure dairy type.
feedingGuide: A mix of grazing, paddy straw, and green fodder works well. Supplement energy when animals are used for field work in wet terrain.
careTips: Pay extra attention to hoof care and fungal skin issues in high-moisture environments. Shelter from prolonged rain improves health.
economicValue: Important in difficult terrains where foot stability, stamina, and adaptability determine farm productivity.

name: Hallikar
description: Hallikar is a lean and athletic South Indian draft breed valued for agility, endurance, and efficient movement across dryland farming regions.
milkYieldInfo: Milk output is modest at around 2 to 5 liters per day because the breed is primarily selected for work capacity rather than dairy specialization.
feedingGuide: Dry fodder, crop residues, and controlled concentrate support are suitable for Hallikar cattle. Working animals benefit from extra energy and mineral support during peak field seasons.
careTips: Maintain hoof care, parasite control, and summer shade. Because Hallikar cattle are active movers, clean dry flooring helps prevent strain and injury.
economicValue: Hallikar remains valuable in breeding and conservation programs focused on premium draft traits, hardiness, and low-input farm utility.

name: Kangayam
description: Kangayam is a celebrated South Indian draft breed known for toughness, efficient movement, and dependable performance in dryland farming.
milkYieldInfo: Milk yield is modest at around 3 to 6 liters per day because breeding emphasis is placed more on work capacity than dairy specialization.
feedingGuide: Dry fodder, crop residues, and seasonal grazing work well. Field-working animals benefit from added energy, salt, and mineral support.
careTips: Maintain hoof care and body condition during long dry periods. Kangayam cattle respond well to shade and clean, well-drained resting space.
economicValue: Highly valuable in conservation and low-input farming systems that prioritize hardiness, breeding quality, and traditional draft utility.

name: Khillari
description: Khillari cattle are agile draft animals from the Deccan plateau, recognized for speed, endurance, and suitability for dry farming landscapes.
milkYieldInfo: Milk production is usually 2 to 5 liters per day, reflecting the breed's stronger orientation toward work than dairying.
feedingGuide: Provide roughage, grazing access, and energy support when animals are used for heavy field work. Minerals and water remain essential in hot months.
careTips: Prevent overwork in peak heat, maintain hoof trimming, and keep housing dry to protect joints and feet on hard ground.
economicValue: A dependable low-input breed for farms that still value field power, endurance, and hardy local genetics.

name: Murrah
description: Murrah is India’s benchmark dairy buffalo breed, famous for high milk volume, rich fat percentage, and broad commercial acceptance.
milkYieldInfo: Well-managed Murrah buffaloes commonly produce 10 to 18 liters a day, with excellent fat content for ghee and paneer markets.
feedingGuide: Needs high-quality green fodder, dry roughage, and concentrate proportional to milk yield. Cooling, wallowing, or sprinklers improve intake.
careTips: Buffaloes are sensitive to heat stress. Provide shade, water, and regular udder hygiene to protect both comfort and yield.
economicValue: One of the most profitable buffalo breeds in organized dairy due to demand for breeding stock and premium-fat milk.

name: Surti
description: Surti buffaloes are medium-framed dairy animals known for good milk fat, manageable size, and suitability for family-scale dairies.
milkYieldInfo: Typical yield is 6 to 10 liters a day with notably rich milk, making the breed attractive for traditional dairy products.
feedingGuide: Balanced fodder, cottonseed cake, and mineral mixture support production well. Provide cooling in hot and humid periods.
careTips: Maintain regular washing and parasite checks. Smaller body size makes them easier to manage but they still need heat relief.
economicValue: A strong fit for farmers who want good-fat milk with moderate feed costs and easier handling than larger buffalo breeds.

name: Mehsana
description: Mehsana buffaloes are productive dairy animals developed in Gujarat and recognized for sustained lactation and strong rural dairy economics.
milkYieldInfo: Average daily milk output ranges from 8 to 14 liters. The breed performs best under structured feeding and regular cooling.
feedingGuide: Green fodder, dry fodder, and protein supplements work well. Maintain clean drinking water and salt-mineral access at all times.
careTips: Heat management is important for consistent conception and milk yield. Maintain clean resting floors to reduce hoof and udder issues.
economicValue: Popular in milk belts because of steady output and strong returns from fat-rich buffalo milk.

name: Jaffarabadi
description: Jaffarabadi is a large-framed buffalo breed valued for size, decent milk output, and strong presence in breed conservation programs.
milkYieldInfo: Milk yield usually stays between 8 and 13 liters per day, with rich buffalo milk suited to value-added dairy processing.
feedingGuide: Large body size calls for generous roughage intake, green fodder, and energy-rich supplements during lactation.
careTips: Provide roomy, non-slippery housing and cooling support. The breed’s size increases the importance of hoof and joint care.
economicValue: Attractive for breeding and dairy where large body frame and high-value stock command premium prices.

name: Bhadawari
description: Bhadawari buffaloes are famous for very high milk fat content and reasonable productivity in dry, hot conditions.
milkYieldInfo: Average milk output is 4 to 8 liters a day, but the breed stands out for fat-rich milk valued in ghee-based markets.
feedingGuide: Use crop residues, green fodder, and oilseed cakes. Buffaloes benefit from regular cooling and uninterrupted water supply.
careTips: Monitor body condition during long dry periods. Maintain vaccination and parasite control, especially in community-grazed setups.
economicValue: Best suited for niche dairy economics where milk fat percentage drives farmer profit more than volume alone.

name: Nili-Ravi
description: Nili-Ravi is a major dairy buffalo type known for high milk yield, good body size, and suitability for intensive dairy settings.
milkYieldInfo: Milk yield commonly ranges from 10 to 16 liters a day with strong performance where nutrition and heat control are managed well.
feedingGuide: Supply protein-rich concentrate, quality fodder, and year-round mineral supplementation. Cooling is essential in hot seasons.
careTips: Watch udder health and reproductive efficiency closely in intensive farms. Buffalo comfort strongly affects milk flow and intake.
economicValue: Highly useful in commercial dairy herds where both volume and fat-rich buffalo milk support profitable marketing.

name: Pandharpuri
description: Pandharpuri buffaloes are recognized by their long horns and good adaptation to the drier districts of Maharashtra.
milkYieldInfo: They generally produce 5 to 9 liters a day and remain useful for rural dairies operating under moderate input conditions.
feedingGuide: Dry fodder with seasonal green fodder works well, but production improves with cottonseed cake or balanced concentrate support.
careTips: Offer shade, clean drinking water, and regular body washing. Horn care and adequate pen space help prevent injuries.
economicValue: An attractive regional dairy buffalo where adaptability and recognizable breed traits strengthen breeding value.

name: Toda
description: Toda buffaloes are an important indigenous hill buffalo breed associated with the Nilgiris, valued for cultural heritage, rich milk, and adaptation to upland conditions.
milkYieldInfo: Milk yield is modest at around 2 to 5 liters per day, but the milk is traditionally valued for richness and specialty use.
feedingGuide: Grazing-based diets with supplemental fodder and minerals support health well. Clean water and weather protection are important in upland climates.
careTips: Preserve strong housing hygiene in wet weather and monitor parasite load in grazing systems. Calm handling helps this smaller population thrive.
economicValue: Important for conservation, heritage breeding, and niche dairy interest tied to indigenous hill livestock systems.

name: Nagpuri
description: Nagpuri buffaloes are drought-resistant animals known for moderate milk yield and utility in harsher agro-climatic zones.
milkYieldInfo: Average milk output ranges from 3 to 7 liters daily, with the breed performing best where toughness and local adaptation are priorities.
feedingGuide: Roughage-based diets are common, with concentrate support during lactation. Plenty of water is necessary in hot weather.
careTips: Keep animals cool and hydrated during dry-season heat. Deworming and timely vaccination are important in grazing systems.
economicValue: Useful for smallholders in semi-arid districts who need a locally adapted buffalo with manageable maintenance requirements.
